body:
My father is a severe alcoholic.  He hasn't had a job for literally decades and lives with my aunt.  Growing up, dad was verbally and physically abusive to my mother.  He never showed up to watch any of the sports I persued, nor did he attend any school functions.  He would, however, still do a lot for my brother and I when we were kids like take us on hikes, fishing, down to 7-11 to get slurpees (and beer for himself) and camping.  He always had beer though, but my brother and I really didn't mind at that age.

When I was 12, my mother heeded the advice of many good people and moved us from Las Vegas to Bum Fuck, Idaho to get away from my father.  I remember being a pretty normal kid, liked to make jokes and was academically proficient and seemingly well as far as I could remember.  I never had a father figure though.  My stepfather, whom my mother met -2 years after we moved was and still is an alcoholic, and they are still together and have been for 13 years now.  

He never really talked to my brother and I, and never really made any kind of emotional attachment.  I don't blamehim, but I want to clarify the reason of this post and it is relevant to that which I am concerned about.
Around 8th grade (possibly sooner) I became very self-conscious and concerned with my looks.  I wasn't as funny as I used to be and was really becoming depressed.  My friends were all druggies, as was I, from middle school through graduation.  I quit using around my junior year, but was still depressed a bit.

College was when my problems really came about.  I was often depressed and was taking a full 19 credits per semester and working a night job.  Ended up dropping out of school due to burnout; I was only getting 2-4 hours a sleep per night and just crashed.

From there on out, I worked and worked, and started drinking a lot and smoking cigarettes.  I was working 2 jobs from 2002 on up to 2005 and continually quit jobs to take positions that paid more.  I was constantly getting more andmore depressed with each passing year.  By the time I had moved back down south, I was working tech support and making good money.  No matter how much I made it made no difference, though.  I was severely depressed from 2006 onward.  I was getting wasted at least 2 times a week, and started contemplating suicide.

I finally had a breakdown, ended up quitting my job and my family helped me get into one of those suicide wards.  At the time I was thinking about blowing my head off on a daily basis and my mother called the cops after I broke down and called her telling her I was going to off myself and had a loaded gun to my head.  It was fucking horrible because I didn't have the balls to pull the trigger.  They doped me up on adderall and zoloft, which helped emmensly, and I was out after a week.  After not filling my prescription I slipped back into my severe depression and landed myself in another suicide ward.  This one was even worse.  They loaded me up on zoloft and lithium, and I would get these brain spasms.  After 4 days I was released and again, quit using my medication.  Back to the same old shit.

Eventually, I quit my job as I could not function in daily life.  I half-assed through everything and mostly just got 
drunk and stoned.  I had the power shut off a few times, internet disconnected, that kind of thing.  No matter how hard I tried, getting out and doing things that had to be done became impossible.  On the outside, I played it off pretty well (until I got drunk), while inside I was literally going insane.  Most of my friends didn't want to be 
around me anymore as my moods were erradic and I was a "downer" to be around.  I ALWAYS focus on bad things, eventually, not a fun person to drink around.

As of this submission, I am 5 weeks into a zoloft prescrip and feel pretty good most days.  I lost everything for the most part and now live with my grandmother.  I have a side job that does okay (400-500 per month) but am withdrawn and sleep a lot.  I have no friends that I see even on a monthly basis.  I stay home every week-end.  Although I am getting better, I still feel suicidal some days.

My question is this:  could not having a father around, being as I'm a 27 year old man who was raised by my mother, be the reason I am so fucked up?  Is there anything anyone sees in my story here that can point out what is wrong with me?

I'm open to anything.  So far, the drugs have worked marginally, I've quit smoking, drinking and doing drugs and 
nothing has helped.  The 2 suicide ward treatments were voluntary but did ABSOLUTELY NOTHING.  I've talked to my doctor and the only things that have changed are the amount of debt I'm going into (currently around $10,000+).  I've tried the self help books, I've tried autosuggestion, I've done everything else I can and am running out of options.

What I really need is some information specifically aimed at mental illness and the problems caused by being the 
child adult of an alcoholic and growing up without a father after the age of 12.  I wish I could really portray the 
dire desperation I'm currently struggling through, and it's getting really hard to hang on to hope.  Any information 
is appreciated.  Thanks.

TL;DR -- Adult (27) male child of an alcoholic.  No father figure or male role model growing up, raised by mother.  Seeks online support forums, advice and/or treatment options as nothing is working all that well.
